text:
## [SECTION 3: The Ritual of Survival]

[SOUND: The heavy, rhythmic thrum of the truck engine becomes the only constant, but it feels muffled, as if the thick fog is swallowing the sound.]

[VISUAL: Close-up of Vikram’s trembling hands holding the weathered paper. The wind howls outside, a mournful, ghostly sound that seems to carry whispers from the peaks.]

[HOST]: (slow) Jaise hi Vikram ne us purane kagaz ko pakda, maahol mein ek bharipan aa gaya. Aisa laga jaise hawa ruk gayi ho... aur sirf uski saansein aur truck ka engine bachenge. [SOUND: A low-frequency drone begins, creating a sense of heavy atmosphere.] Wo diary ke panno ko palatne laga, jahan har niyam ek warning tha—ek boundary jo use maut aur zindagi ke beech khadi kar rahi thi.

[VISUAL: Slow zoom on the text in the manual. The paper is yellowed, and the ink looks like dried blood.]

[HOST]: Vikram ne pehla rule padha. [pause] 
"Rule Number One: Agar hawaon mein maa ki awaaz sunai de... toh uska jawab mat dena." (slow)

[SOUND: A faint, distorted female voice is heard in the wind for a split second, then cut by a sudden gust of air.]

[HOST]: Vikram ke shareer mein ek jhatka laga. Usne socha shayad ye sirf ek purani kahani hai, par us pal, us thandi dhund mein, use aisa laga jaise koi sach mein uska naam pukaar raha ho. Par usne aankhein band kar li.

[VISUAL: Cut to a wide shot of the truck's cabin, illuminated only by the dashboard lights.]

[HOST]: Agla rule... (pause)
"Rule Number Two: Agar dhund ka rang peela ho jaye, toh sirf high-beam lights ka istemal karein." 

[SOUND: A subtle shift in the background music—a metallic, unsettling drone.]

[HOST]: Vikram ne bahar dekha. Dhund ki ek leher uske cabin ke paas se guzri... aur usme ek ajeeb sa, sunehra peela rang chamka. Usne kaanpte hathon se high-beam on kiya. Raasta thoda saaf hua, par darr kam nahi hua.

[HOST]: Rule Number Three: "Agar peeche wale mirror mein cabin ki chhat par koi saya dikhe... toh uski taraf mat dekhna." (slow)

[SOUND: A heavy metallic 'thud'—like something heavy landing on a roof.]

[HOST]: Vikram ki saans atak gayi. Usne mirror ki taraf dekhne ki koshish ki, lekin rule yaad aaya. Use pata tha ki agar usne dekha, toh shayad wo kabhi mudeh nahi payega. 

[VISUAL: Close-up of the rearview mirror. It's empty for now, but the shadow of a tree or structure passes over it.]

[HOST]: Rule Number Four: "Agar kisi ne truck ke lohe ke darwaze par dastak di... use bilkul ignore karein." (slow)

[SOUND: A slow, deliberate 'thud... thud...' on the metal door of the cabin. It sounds like a heavy fist.]

[HOST]: [pause] Vikram ne apni ungliyan kas kar steering wheel par jad liye. Bahar koi nahi tha... ya kam se kam, wo kuch aisa tha jo insani nahi lag raha tha. 

[VISUAL: The camera focuses on the door handle, which vibrates slightly as if someone is leaning against it.]

[HOST]: Jaise-jaise woh aage badha, rules aur bhi khatarnaak hote gaye. Aise jaise har naya rule ek nayi darr ki deewar khadi kar raha tha. 

[HOST]: Rule Number Five: "Agar aapki peripheral vision mein koi aninvited mehman dikhe... toh unse baat na karein." (slow)

[HOST]: Vikram ko apne side seat ke kone mein kuch hilta hua dikha. Ek saaya, jo dhundhli si roshni mein bas ek munsalik shape ki tarah tha. 

[HOLD: Silence for 2 seconds.]

[HOST]: Rule Number Six: "Agar koi saaya gaadi ke saath-saath chalte hue dikhe... toh raftaar kam mat karein." (slow)

[SOUND: The sound of heavy footsteps on gravel, keeping pace with the truck’s movement.]

[HOST]: Woh daud raha tha. Ya shayad woh uske sath chal raha tha. Ek maut ka khel jo sirf ek pal mein khatam ho sakta tha. 

[VISUAL: A blurry silhouette of a tall figure walking alongside the truck in the white-out conditions.]

[HOST]: Rule Number Seven: "Agar engine poori khamoshi mein ruk jaye, toh restart karne se pehle teen minute tak mantra ya prarthana karein." (slow)

[SOUND: The engine suddenly dies. Total silence follows—only the wind remains.]

[HOST]: [pause] Teen minute ka wo waqt Vikram ke liye sadiyon jaisa tha. Har pal use lag raha tha ki koi uske cabin ke bahar khada hai, intezar kar raha hai ki kab woh galti kare. 

[SOUND: A low-frequency hum builds and then suddenly the engine roars back to life.]

[HOST]: Rule Number Eight: "Raste par rakhi gayi 'Paani' ki botalon ko hath na lagayein." (slow)

[VISUAL: Quick cuts of water bottles left at small roadside shrines, some covered in dust, some looking freshly placed.]

[HOST]: Ye paani unke liye tha... jo pichle raaste par kho gaye the. Ya shayad unke liye jo abhi bhi wahan ghoom rahe hain.

[HOST]: Rule Number Nine: "Agar raat ke waqt raste par koi bachcha dikhe, toh apni nazar sirf samne ke raaste par rakhein." (slow)

[SOUND: A faint sound of a child crying in the distance.]

[HOST]: Yeh sabse mushkil tha. Ek maa ka dil... ek insaan ki fitrat... lekin Gata Loops par, maano hona hi maut ko dawat dena tha. 

[VISUAL: The truck's headlights illuminate a small figure standing by the road, but it's barely visible through the fog.]

[HOST]: Rule Number Ten: "Agar radio par aapke past ka koi music bajne lage, toh use turant band kar dein." (slow)

[SOUND: A distorted, crackling old Bollywood song plays for a second before being cut off by static.]

[HOST]: Kuch cheezein purani hoti hain... aur kuch yaadein unhe zinda rakhti hain. Vikram ko nahi pata tha ki wo music kahan se aa raha hai. 

[VISUAL: The radio dial flickering with static.]

[HOST]: Rule Number Eleven: "Har baar jab kisi shrine (mandir) ke paas se guzrein, toh do baar horn bajayein taaki apni maujoodgi ka elaan ho sake." (slow)

[SOUND: Two sharp, loud horn blasts that echo through the mountains.]

[HOST]: Ye ek warning thi. Ek signal ki 'hum' yahan hain... aur humein rasta pata hai. 

[HOLD: A long pause of 3 seconds before the final rule.]

[HOST]: Aur aakhri niyam... jo sabse zyada bhayankar tha. Rule Number Twelve: "Agar aapko apne cabin ki chhat par koi khada dikhe... toh upar mat dekhiye." (slow)

[SOUND: A high-pitched, metallic scraping sound on the roof of the truck.]

[HOST]: [pause] Vikram ne apni aankhein band kar li. Uska dil itni zor se dhadak raha tha ki wo uske kaanon mein goonj rahi thi. 

[VISUAL: Close up of Vikram's face, sweating and terrified.]

[HOST]: Tabhi... (slow) ek awaaz aayi. Ek kharachili, bhari awaaz ne darwaze par dastak di. "Beta... zara ruko."

[SOUND: A heavy thud on the door, followed by the sound of scratching metal.]

[HOST]: Vikram ka haath handle ki taraf badha. Uska dimaag chilla raha tha—*Rule Number Four!* Par uski body kaanp rahi thi. Use laga jaise woh awaaz kisi aise shakhs ki hai jise madad chahiye. Ek majboor insaan ki awaaz.

[SOUND: A low, guttural growl blends into the sound of the wind.]

[HOST]: Usne darwaza kholne hi wala tha... jab usne yaad kiya—Rule Number Twelve. Agar tumne dekha, toh woh tumhe dekh lega. 

[VISUAL: The camera shakes as a heavy thud hits the roof again, and the metal of the cabin groans.]

[HOST]: Us raat, Gata Loops ki dhund mein, Vikram ko samajh aa gaya... ke ye rules uski hifazat ke liye nahi the. Ye un cheezon ko rokne ke liye the, jo raste par kabza karna chahti thi. 

[SOUND: A sudden, sharp crack of a branch breaking nearby.]

[HOST]: Aur ab... jab humein lagta hai ki ye sab sirf ek kahani hai, toh asliyat aur dhund ke beech ka farq mita dena mushkil ho jata hai.
summary: In this section, the atmosphere intensifies as Vikram encounters the 12 survival rules, which escalate from environmental warnings to terrifying supernatural encounters, culminating in a moment where he must resist the urge to respond to a voice outside his truck.
